name: APC Smart-UPS SMT3000RMI2U · 2U · AP9640 NMC3
source: MODEL (user-confirmed): APC Smart-UPS SMT3000RMI2U (no SmartConnect; the rear model label also reads "SMT3000RMI2U"). Official Schneider Electric product page for SMT3000RMI2U (https://www.se.com/au/en/product/SMT3000RMI2U/apc-smartups-line-interactive-3kva-rackmount-2u-230v-8x-iec-c13+1x-iec-c19-outlets-smartslot-avr-lcd/, Australia; the UK page redirects to the product catalogue): 2U, height 86 mm, width 480 mm, depth 683 mm, product weight 44.28 kg, 8 × IEC C13 + 1 × IEC C19 outputs, C20 input, one free SmartSlot, 3000 VA / 2700 W, mounting mode "Rack-mounted with included kit", provided equipment includes "Rack mounting support rails", two-post mountable 0. heightMm 86 and massKg 44.28 are taken from that page (datasheet). The closely related SMT3000RMI2UC brochure (https://ckm-content.se.com/ckmContent/sfc/servlet.shepherd/document/download/0691H00000FWcBtQAL) gives 86.1 mm and 44.28 kg; it is no longer used for this model. DEPTH DATUM (user-entered, approximate): 670 mm OVERALL from the front of the bezel to the very rear of the unit, with the ear flanges about 630 mm from the rear. depthMm is therefore 630 mm (ear plane to rear panel) and the front bezel is a separate solid projecting about 40 mm forward of the ear plane (z = -40 to 0 mm). The datasheet 683 mm depth does not match the 670 mm overall (possibly rear fittings or the bezel profile; not resolved). The bezel needs at least 40 mm of clear depth in front of the mounting rails on the face it is mounted to; in a rear-mounted position it projects 40 mm behind the rear rails. WIDTH: body 430 mm (user-entered; the width tape reads 43 cm) inside 482.6 mm (19-inch) ears (user-entered). 480 mm is the datasheet width, not the body width. The front bezel solid is 430 × 86 × 40 mm (projection user-entered, approximate; width and height ASSUMED equal to the body, PROVISIONAL). FRONT (user photos and a product image, layout only, not embedded): the bezel carries the APC logo, a slotted grille and the LCD panel with five buttons on the right as seen from the front. These are controls, not cable endpoints, and are not modelled. Front face features are not added because they would render behind the bezel solid. The panel note "FOR BATTERY REPLACEMENT REMOVE FRONT BEZEL" means the bezel must be removable in place. REAR: rear port X centres are user-entered tape readings from photos 18 to 21 (approximate, about ±3 mm); every Y centre and the AP9640 connector centres remain provisional (see each port). The rear perforated cover plate is a visual grille only (position provisional). The overload protector (push-to-reset button, about 80-83 mm right of centre as viewed from behind in photos 20 and 21) and the earth screw beside the model label are not cable endpoints and are not modelled. No serial number, site or workplace detail from the photos is recorded. EARS (user-entered): the ear screws use the bottom and middle holes of U1 and the middle and top holes of U2, so screwOffsetsMm are 6.35, 22.225, 66.675 (44.45 + 22.225) and 82.55 (44.45 + 38.1) mm above the device bottom. Ear thickness unknown (2 mm illustrative preview). MOUNTING (user-entered; rails also listed as provided equipment on the official page): the UPS is always installed on the support rails supplied with it, unless it stands on the floor. One fixed, non-sliding L-section rail per side sits just behind the rack screw holes (inside the rack-rail plane) and is screwed to the front and rear rack rails; the UPS rests on the horizontal flange, small rear tabs on the UPS slot into the rear of each rail, and the UPS is screwed in at the front through its ears. Rail dimensions, part number and front-to-rear adjustment range are unknown (no spare set to measure). mounting stays "direct" (the ears are modelled and screwed at the front) because Rack Studio's "rails" mounting requires a sourced railMinMm/railMaxMm and, with them null, the app refuses to place the unit. The support rails are NOT modelled. SCHEMA GAP: Rack Studio has no fixed L-section support rail; its only rail assembly is the per-placement sliding (telescoping) rail at the chassis sides, which cannot sit under the chassis, carries no load rating and has no rear-tab engagement. POWER: rating label (user photo) "MAX OUTPUT POWER RATING 3000VA/2700W" for the 3000 VA model, input 220-240 V 50/60 Hz, maximum input current 16 A. Banks: GROUP 1 (8 × C13, 10 A per receptacle group as printed) and the C19 output (16 A as printed), both at 230 V nominal within the printed 220-240 V range. SCHEMA GAP: the UPS total output limit (3000 VA, about 13.0 A at 230 V; 2700 W) cannot be expressed because power banks are independent, so the two banks together allow 26 A; check the total against 2700 W by hand. The UPS own draw (losses and battery charging; the official page lists 182 W rated battery charging power) is not set. EXPANSION: an APC AP9640 Network Management Card 3 is fitted in the SmartSlot (user-supplied configuration), printed text the right way up and the RJ45 latch on top (user-confirmed). Its Network RJ45 and Console micro-USB are modelled as rear ports at provisional positions inside the measured slot opening.

powerBanks.name: Group 1 (8 × C13)
powerBanks.source: Printed on the rear panel beside the outlets (user photo): "GROUP 1" and "OUTPUT: 220-240V, 50/60Hz, 10A PER RECEPTACLE GROUP". The bank limit is the printed 10 A group rating; no separate per-outlet rating is printed, so the per-outlet limit is set to the same 10 A. 230 V is the nominal value within the printed 220–240 V range. This bank is independent of the C19 bank: the UPS total output limit (3000 VA / 2700 W) is NOT enforced across banks (schema gap).

powerBanks.name: C19 output
powerBanks.source: Printed on the rear panel above the C19 outlet (user photo): "OUTPUT: 220-240V, 50/60Hz, 16A". 230 V is the nominal value within the printed 220–240 V range. This bank is independent of GROUP 1: the UPS total output limit (3000 VA / 2700 W) is NOT enforced across banks (schema gap).

ports.name: NMC Network · RJ45
ports.source: SmartSlot opening: user-entered from the tape in photo 18 (hook at the left edge of the rear panel as viewed from behind, tape along the top edge). The opening reads about 15.5 mm to 115.5 mm from the left edge, so the card face spans x = -199.5 to -99.5 mm with its centre at x = -149.5 mm (about 100 mm wide; approximate, about ±3 mm). An APC AP9640 Network Management Card 3 is fitted in it (user-supplied configuration; the slot is empty in the photos). User-confirmed orientation: the card is fitted with its printed text the right way up, so, as seen from behind, Console (micro-USB) is to the left of Network (RJ45), with the Reset pinhole to the right of the RJ45, matching the user's AP9640 product image. On that faceplate both connectors sit in the right-hand half, so both placeholders are placed right of the measured card-face centre (less negative X). PROVISIONAL placeholder centre within the measured slot (x -120, y 66 are round numbers, not measured and not scaled from either photo); the card's connector positions were not on the tape. Latch orientation (user-confirmed): the RJ45 clip (latch) is on the TOP of the connector. Recorded as rotationDeg 180: Rack Studio's RJ45 face glyph draws the latch keyway at the bottom at 0° (as on the UPS SERIAL jack), and rotationDeg is clockwise roll viewed from outside the socket, so 180° puts the keyway on top. Rotation does not change the port centre, footprint or cable direction. Aperture size is the designer palette default. Labelled "Network" with "10/100/1000" printed on the AP9640 faceplate (user product image); no PoE or other capability is inferred.
